rv.q: But the whole of 'Safe House' feels distant, and that isn't Gilmore's doing. There's no losing ourselves in the play, no entering Grace's story, because she isn't even a symbol, really, but rather an abstraction...
Attending Safe House is an immersive, hypnotic experience filled with haunting song, spell-binding spectacle, and an undercurrent of feeling.
As a concept album, I buy it; as a work of theater, I wanted more humanity and more of Grace's agency in the mix.

vr.q: I think if you're open to something that requires that level of engagement or you like experimental pieces that demand dissection and interpretation, this is for you.
